description: Frontmatter parity between the TS writer/reader (yaml@2.9.1, serializeProperties) and the Rust reader (parse_frontmatter).

Each case: `yaml` is the frontmatter body without delimiters. Rust parses "---
" + yaml + "
---
" and must equal `rustExpected ?? expected`.

TS: when `properties` is set, serializeProperties(properties) must equal `yaml`. Unless `rustOnly`, yaml.parse(yaml, { uniqueKeys: false }) must throw when `tsThrows`, otherwise its projection (keys through canonicalizeKey, maps nested at any depth become null) must equal `tsExpected ?? expected`.
`fallback: true` marks input yaml-rust2 rejects; the Rust value then comes from the line-based subset parser.
`divergence` explains a case where Rust and yaml@2.9.1 are known to read the same bytes differently.

sentinels.__INFINITY__: Stands for a non-finite number (Infinity), which JSON cannot hold. Only used in tsExpected.

cases.name: plain scalars
cases.yaml:
title: Example
author: me
count: 7
draft: true
rating: 4.5

cases.name: literal block scalar with strip chomping
cases.yaml:
notes: |-
  line one
  line two
after: x

cases.name: literal block scalar with clip chomping as the last line
literal block scalar with indentation indicator
flow list item with a comma
relationship to a note with a comma
nested map is null and siblings are kept
cases.yaml:
parent:
  child1: value1
  child2: value2
sibling: hello

cases.name: empty value is null, quoted empty is an empty string
null and boolean spellings
cases.yaml:
a: null
b: Null
c: NULL
d: ~
e: True
f: TRUE
g: false

cases.name: yes, quoted numbers and dates stay strings
duplicate keys are last-wins
cases.yaml:
key: first
key: second
key: third

cases.name: empty key is skipped
cases.divergence: yaml@2.9.1 keeps the entry under the empty key; Rust skips it, as the subset parser did.

cases.name: keys go through canonicalize_key
cases.yaml:
type: event
color: blue
event_color: red

cases.name: block list with a lone dash
non-decimal and special numeric forms
cases.divergence: Plain scalars resolve through parse_scalar in Rust, so hex, octal and .inf stay strings; yaml@2.9.1 reads them as numbers.

cases.name: integer above 2^53 stays exact
cases.divergence: Rust keeps integers above 2^53 exact; JSON.parse in the TS test runner rounds them, so the case is Rust-only.

cases.name: unquoted wikilinks in a flow list
cases.divergence: Rust projects a sequence holding exactly one sequence holding exactly one scalar X to "[[X]]"; yaml@2.9.1 returns nested arrays.

cases.name: single unquoted wikilink
cases.divergence: See the unquoted wikilink rule above.

cases.name: unquoted wikilink as a block item
cases.divergence: See the unquoted wikilink rule above.

cases.name: block list holding one single-item flow list
cases.divergence: The unquoted wikilink rule matches the shape, not the spelling: a block list whose only item is a one-item flow list also becomes "[[X]]"; yaml@2.9.1 returns nested arrays.

cases.name: comment after a value is dropped
plain scalar continues on a more indented line
block list at the key indentation
map inside a list is null
anchors and aliases resolve
cases.yaml:
a: &x hello
b: *x
m: &y
  k: v
n: *y
l: &z [1, 2]
o: *z

cases.name: null as a key
cases.divergence: Rust keys are the scalar text; yaml@2.9.1 resolves the key to null and stores it under the empty key.

cases.name: explicit str tag
cases.divergence: Rust ignores tags, so a tagged plain scalar still resolves through parse_scalar.

cases.name: fallback: nested colon in a plain value
fallback: line without a colon
cases.yaml:
valid: yes
this is not valid yaml
another: ok
